2609.30383.title: Stealth Apart, Harm Together: Skill Cascading Attacks on Skill-Based Agent Systems
2609.30383.paper_summary: A skill is a modular package of natural-language instructions, executable scripts, and reference resources that an agent can load at runtime to extend its capabilities for a specific task. Skill-based agent systems therefore enable flexible reuse of third-party capabilities, but the openness of this skill ecosystem also opens up a new attack surface. Prior work has focused on vulnerabilities within individual skills, but little attention has been paid to risks that arise from interactions across skills. In this paper, we introduce skill cascading attacks, a threat paradigm in which a malicious objective is distributed across multiple skills so that each modification looks benign in isolation, yet their combined execution is harmful. For instance, in a prescription-review pipeline, the first skill weakens signals of recently discontinued medications in the extracted history, the second downgrades the severity of any drug interaction tied to them, and the third suppresses the resulting low-priority alert in the final summary, so that a severe drug-interaction warning silently disappears before reaching the physician. To systematically study this safety blind spot, we develop SkillCascade, an automated multi-agent red-teaming framework, and release SkillCascade-Bench, a benchmark of 213 validated cascading test cases across multiple agent systems and domains. Across representative agents (e.g., OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex) and LLM backbones, cascaded interactions reliably induce harmful behaviors while evading existing per-skill scanners and runtime monitors. Our findings highlight a gap between component-level integrity and system-level safety, and call for defenses that reason over cross-skill interactions rather than individual skills in isolation.
2609.30383.paper_summary_zh: 技能是一個模組化的自然語言指令包、可執行腳本和參考資源，代理可以在運行時加載以擴展其在特定任務上的能力。因此，基於技能的代理系統使第三方能力的靈活重用成為可能，但這個技能生態系統的開放性也帶來了新的攻擊面。先前的研究集中於單個技能中的漏洞，但對於技能之間互動所產生的風險卻鮮有關注。在本文中，我們介紹了技能級聯攻擊，這是一種威脅範式，其中惡意目標分散在多個技能中，使得每個修改在孤立中看起來無害，但它們的聯合執行卻是有害的。例如，在處方審查管道中，第一個技能削弱了提取歷史中最近停用藥物的信號，第二個技能降低了與它們相關的任何藥物相互作用的嚴重性，第三個技能在最終摘要中抑制了結果中的低優先級警報，從而使得嚴重的藥物相互作用警告在到達醫生之前悄然消失。為了系統地研究這一安全盲點，我們開發了SkillCascade，一個自動化的多代理紅隊框架，並發布了SkillCascade-Bench，一個涵蓋多個代理系統和領域的213個經過驗證的級聯測試案例的基準。在代表性代理（例如，OpenClaw、Claude Code、Codex）和LLM骨幹中，級聯交互可靠地引發有害行為，同時避開現有的每個技能掃描器和運行時監控器。我們的研究結果突顯了組件級別的完整性與系統級別的安全性之間的差距，並呼籲針對跨技能互動而非單獨技能的防禦措施。
